principles: Preserve historical evidence rather than rewriting old memory text.
Make current Proofbound/Lattice guidance mechanically preferred in host preflight.
Keep dev-memory explicitly non-authoritative and outside gate evidence.
drivers: Old Koala wording can mislead future hosts if surfaced as active guidance.
Users need a reviewable table/output showing which memories are current versus legacy.
Implementation should be small and avoid broad branding cleanup.

options.name: A: computed supersession projection over existing memory fields
pros: Can rank superseding entries first and annotate superseded entries
cons: Old raw JSON still contains legacy wording

options.name: B: rewrite legacy memory entries in place
pros: Raw memory text becomes clean immediately
cons: Harder to audit what actually happened
Risky for global memory shared across contexts

options.name: C: add only new superseding memories without code changes
cons: Preflight/search may still surface old Koala entries first
Does not solve the host-misleading behavior mechanically

chosen: A: computed supersession projection over existing memory fields
rationale: Option A gives the behavior the user wants without falsifying history: old Koala memories remain auditable, but current Proofbound/Lattice entries can rank first and mark legacy entries as superseded in visible outputs.

preMortem.scenario: A future host still follows a Koala memory as active guidance
preMortem.trigger: Preflight/search returns a legacy Koala entry before the superseding Proofbound entry
preMortem.consequence: Host uses stale names or wrong reviewer labels
preMortem.mitigation: Add supersession-aware ordering and visible superseded annotations with smoke coverage.

preMortem.scenario: Cleanup rewrites or deletes historical evidence
preMortem.trigger: Implementation edits global JSONL old rows directly
preMortem.consequence: Audit trail is weakened and old evidenceRefs become misleading
preMortem.mitigation: Only append superseding entries and compute projection metadata at read/search/preflight time.

preMortem.scenario: Supersession mechanism looks like gate evidence
preMortem.trigger: New fields or docs imply memory can satisfy DONE/review gates
preMortem.mitigation: Keep authority non_authoritative, gateEvidence false, and document supersession as advisory context only.
